exam_guide_revision: Not a certification. Practical Python 3.10-3.14 fluency track; official Python documentation and selected AnyIO/HTTPX docs reviewed 2026-09-19.

learning_design.unlock_rule: A knowledge node unlocks after all required prompts are revealed.
learning_design.mastery_note: Discovery progress is not mastery evidence; progressively harder typed code recall provides the scored signal.

authoring_notes: Python Fluency is practical coding retrieval, not beginner trivia or a certification. Questions use progressive recall depth: guided -> recall -> construct -> fluency. Short literals stay on one line where readable, unfamiliar data shapes and intent are explained, and most questions have one meaningful blank.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: __________ calls a factory to create a missing value automatically, which is useful when grouping or accumulating.

reveal.text: collections.defaultdict calls a factory to create a missing value automatically, which is useful when grouping or accumulating.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: __________(list) lets groups[key].append(value) work without a separate initialization branch.

reveal.text: defaultdict(list) lets groups[key].append(value) work without a separate initialization branch.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: __________ the factory itself, such as list, not list(); calling it eagerly would pass a list object instead of a callable.

reveal.text: Pass the factory itself, such as list, not list(); calling it eagerly would pass a list object instead of a callable.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: __________ counts hashable values and most_common(n) returns the n most frequent element-count pairs.

reveal.text: collections.Counter counts hashable values and most_common(n) returns the n most frequent element-count pairs.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: __________(events).most_common(2) is the direct idiom for the top two event types.

reveal.text: Counter(events).most_common(2) is the direct idiom for the top two event types.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: __________ is a dict subclass; a missing key reads as zero, but zero-count entries can still remain stored.

reveal.text: Counter is a dict subclass; a missing key reads as zero, but zero-count entries can still remain stored.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: __________ supports O(1)-style appends and pops from both ends and is a natural in-memory FIFO queue.

reveal.text: collections.deque supports O(1)-style appends and pops from both ends and is a natural in-memory FIFO queue.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: __________(item) with queue.popleft() processes items in arrival order.

reveal.text: queue.append(item) with queue.popleft() processes items in arrival order.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: __________(0) shifts remaining list elements; deque.popleft() is the usual choice for repeated front removals.

reveal.text: list.pop(0) shifts remaining list elements; deque.popleft() is the usual choice for repeated front removals.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: __________(key, default) returns the existing value or inserts and returns the provided default when the key is absent.

reveal.text: dict.setdefault(key, default) returns the existing value or inserts and returns the provided default when the key is absent.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: __________(team, []).append(user) is a compact grouping idiom when a defaultdict is not desired.

reveal.text: groups.setdefault(team, []).append(user) is a compact grouping idiom when a defaultdict is not desired.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: __________ default expression is evaluated before setdefault is called, so avoid expensive defaults in a hot path when they are usually unused.

reveal.text: The default expression is evaluated before setdefault is called, so avoid expensive defaults in a hot path when they are usually unused.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: __________() and max() accept key= for comparison logic, and the single-iterable form can accept default= for empty input.

reveal.text: min() and max() accept key= for comparison logic, and the single-iterable form can accept default= for empty input.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: __________(users, key=lambda u: u.score, default=None) returns the highest-scoring user or None when users is empty.

reveal.text: max(users, key=lambda u: u.score, default=None) returns the highest-scoring user or None when users is empty.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: __________= is accepted only with the iterable form, not when passing multiple positional candidates.

reveal.text: default= is accepted only with the iterable form, not when passing multiple positional candidates.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: __________() short-circuits when an item is truthy, while all() short-circuits when an item is falsy; generator expressions avoid building a temporary list.

reveal.text: any() short-circuits when an item is truthy, while all() short-circuits when an item is falsy; generator expressions avoid building a temporary list.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: __________(user.active for user in users) verifies every user lazily.

reveal.text: all(user.active for user in users) verifies every user lazily.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: __________([]) is True and any([]) is False, which matters when an empty collection should have different business meaning.

reveal.text: all([]) is True and any([]) is False, which matters when an empty collection should have different business meaning.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: __________(key, default) reads a value without raising KeyError and returns the supplied default when the key is absent.

reveal.text: dict.get(key, default) reads a value without raising KeyError and returns the supplied default when the key is absent.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: __________ = config.get('timeout', 30) keeps the fallback close to the lookup.

reveal.text: timeout = config.get('timeout', 30) keeps the fallback close to the lookup.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: __________() cannot distinguish a missing key from a present key whose stored value equals the chosen default; use membership testing when that distinction matters.

reveal.text: get() cannot distinguish a missing key from a present key whose stored value equals the chosen default; use membership testing when that distinction matters.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: __________(sep) always returns a three-tuple: text before the separator, the separator itself, and text after it.

reveal.text: str.partition(sep) always returns a three-tuple: text before the separator, the separator itself, and text after it.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: __________, sep, rest = url.partition('://') is useful when the separator's presence also matters.

reveal.text: scheme, sep, rest = url.partition('://') is useful when the separator's presence also matters.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: __________ the separator is absent, partition returns (original, '', ''), unlike split() which returns a variable-length list.

reveal.text: When the separator is absent, partition returns (original, '', ''), unlike split() which returns a variable-length list.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: __________(prefix) and removesuffix(suffix) remove an exact affix when present without treating the argument as a set of characters.

reveal.text: str.removeprefix(prefix) and removesuffix(suffix) remove an exact affix when present without treating the argument as a set of characters.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: __________('test_') removes only that literal prefix.

reveal.text: name.removeprefix('test_') removes only that literal prefix.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: __________()/lstrip()/rstrip() remove characters from a set at an edge; they are not substitutes for removing an exact prefix or suffix.

reveal.text: strip()/lstrip()/rstrip() remove characters from a set at an edge; they are not substitutes for removing an exact prefix or suffix.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: __________ operators express membership relationships directly: & for intersection, | for union, - for difference, and ^ for symmetric difference.

reveal.text: Set operators express membership relationships directly: & for intersection, | for union, - for difference, and ^ for symmetric difference.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: __________ = required_fields - payload.keys() finds required keys that are absent from a mapping.

reveal.text: missing = required_fields - payload.keys() finds required keys that are absent from a mapping.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: __________ operations discard ordering and duplicates; use another structure when either is semantically important.

reveal.text: Set operations discard ordering and duplicates; use another structure when either is semantically important.
